evidence: Verg. A. 7.637: it bellō tessera signum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: In the army a tessera was the tablet with the night’s watchword, and so the watchword itself (Lewis & Short). Traupman uses it for a computer’s password. Classically also a die (Cic. Sen. 58).

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 261, 357.
